name: AnthropicAgentAdapter
summary: Adapts concise context for Claude Sonnet, Opus, and Haiku. Detection: matches when ClientInfo.Name is "claude-code" or "claude-ai", or when the model hint contains "claude", "sonnet", "opus", or "haiku". Formatting strategy: - Wraps sections in XML tags for structured context parsing - Orders stable content first (summary → files) for prompt-cache eligibility - Haiku: aggressive trimming, no decoration - Opus: larger token budget, adds a block

name: AnthropicContextFormatter
summary:
Formats raw concise context into Claude-optimised XML-tagged sections. Raw context structure (parts joined with "

" by LocalContextService): [optional] "Summary:
{text}" [optional] "Requested files: {csv}" [0-5] recent history strings [1] the user prompt (last element) Output structure (stable parts first for prompt-cache eligibility): … — summary if present … — file list if present … — recent history if present … — the user prompt [Opus only] …

name: HaikuPreprocess
summary: Reduces token count for Haiku by: - Stripping single-line code comments (// …, # …) from inline code snippets - Collapsing runs of 3+ blank lines to a single blank line - Removing trailing whitespace per line

name: AnthropicVariant
summary: Distinguishes Claude model tiers within the Anthropic family. Each variant gets a different `ContextFormat` (token budget, trimming aggressiveness) and may receive extra blocks in the adapted context.

name: AdapterKind
summary: Classifies an IAgentAdapter as detecting the calling client application (Cursor, Copilot, Continue — determines behavioural flags like WillAskForMissingContext) versus the underlying AI model (Claude, Qwen, DeepSeek — determines prompt formatting). Both kinds can match simultaneously; ResolveBoth returns one of each so their ContextFormats can be merged.

name: IAgentAdapter
summary: Adapts raw concise context for a specific AI model family or client application. Implementations are registered via AddAdapter{TAdapter} and resolved through AgentAdapterRegistry.

name: ICallerDetectionService
summary: Detects the calling AI client and model from an inbound MCP request. Detection waterfall (first match wins): 1. mcpClientName / mcpClientVersion — from IMcpServer.ClientInfo, extracted by the caller before calling Detect (avoids a hard reference to the MCP package in this library). 2. X-Model-Hint or X-LLM-Model request header — explicit model name set by the client. 3. User-Agent request header — last-resort string match. 4. TokenSaverConfig.OllamaModel — used when our own Ollama stack is the caller. 5. Safe-default CallerInfo with empty strings. Call this on every tool invocation; detection is pure string matching with no I/O.

name: AgentHelpersServiceExtensions
summary: DI registration helpers for TokenSaver.AgentHelpers.

name: AddAgentHelpers
summary: Registers AgentHelpers core services. ollamaModelName should be the value of `TokenSaverConfig.OllamaModel` — it is used as the lowest-priority caller detection signal when no MCP ClientInfo or headers are present. Usage in Program.cs: builder.Services .AddAgentHelpers(config.OllamaModel) .AddAdapter() .AddAdapter() .AddAdapter() .AddAdapter();

name: AddAdapter
summary: Registers a concrete IAgentAdapter implementation. Chain multiple calls to register all adapter libraries.

name: CallerInfo
summary: Identifies the AI client and model that sent the current MCP request. Populated by CallerDetectionService from a waterfall of signals: 1. IMcpServer.ClientInfo (from MCP initialize handshake, may be null in stateless mode) 2. X-Model-Hint / X-LLM-Model request header 3. User-Agent request header 4. TokenSaverConfig.OllamaModel (when our own Ollama stack is the caller) 5. Safe-default fallback

name: ClientName
summary: Client application name from the MCP initialize handshake, e.g. "claude-code", "cursor".
code: public string ClientName { get; init; } = "";

name: ClientVersion
summary: Client application version from the MCP initialize handshake.
code: public string? ClientVersion { get; init; }

name: ModelHint
summary: Explicit model name hint — from X-Model-Hint header, X-LLM-Model header, or TokenSaverConfig.OllamaModel. Lower-cased before storage. Examples: "claude-sonnet-4-6", "deepseek-r1", "qwen2.5-coder", "llama3.2"
code: public string? ModelHint { get; init; }

name: UserAgent
summary: Raw User-Agent header value. Used as a last-resort signal.
code: public string? UserAgent { get; init; }

name: Source
summary: Which detection signal actually produced this CallerInfo. Useful for logging and diagnostics.
code: public DetectionSource Source { get; init; } = DetectionSource.Default;

name: ContextFormat
summary: Describes how a specific AI model family prefers to receive context. Produced by GetFormat and consumed by AdaptContext and by LocalContextService.

name: Default
summary: Safe defaults used when no adapter matches.

name: AnthropicSonnet
summary: Format for Anthropic Sonnet — balanced, XML sections, 80K budget.

name: AnthropicOpus
summary: Format for Anthropic Opus — same as Sonnet but larger budget.

name: AnthropicHaiku
summary: Format for Anthropic Haiku — aggressive trimming, short prompts.

name: Qwen
summary: Format for Qwen 2.5 / 3.x — output schema + self-check, Markdown headers.

name: DeepSeekR1
summary: Format for DeepSeek R1 — no system prompt, minimal, no CoT.

name: DeepSeekV3
summary: Format for DeepSeek V3 / Coder — XML + Markdown, system prompt OK.

name: Llama
summary: Format for Llama 3 — Markdown headers, standard system prompt, conservative budget.

name: Mistral
summary: Format for Mistral — short focused prompts, bullets, conservative budget.

name: Gemma
summary: Format for Gemma — system context embedded in first user turn, no separate system prompt.

name: Copilot
summary: Format for GitHub Copilot (VS Code extension / Copilot Chat). Copilot silently drops content by relevance priority above its output-buffer threshold (~8 K tokens per tool response) and will NOT ask for missing content. Keep responses short and always label summaries explicitly.

name: Continue
summary: Format for Continue.dev. Continue errors when a file context provider returns content above ~12 K tokens and will NOT request missing content. Split or skip large files.

name: Cursor
summary: Format for Cursor. Cursor writes large tool output to temp files and re-reads selectively, so it CAN discover missing content — but sends a lossy summarisation after context fills. Always label summaries; prefer full files over many summaries to avoid post-fill degradation.

name: UseXmlSectionTags
summary: Wrap major context sections in XML tags, e.g. …. Best for: Anthropic models, DeepSeek V3/Coder.
code: public bool UseXmlSectionTags { get; init; }

name: UseMarkdownHeaders
summary: Use Markdown ## headers to separate context sections. Best for: Qwen, Llama, Mistral, Gemma, DeepSeek V3/Coder.
code: public bool UseMarkdownHeaders { get; init; } = true;

name: SupportsSystemPrompt
summary: True if the model handles a separate system prompt correctly. False means context must be folded into the first user message. Set to false for: DeepSeek R1, Gemma.
code: public bool SupportsSystemPrompt { get; init; } = true;

name: AvoidChainOfThought
summary: True for reasoning models (DeepSeek R1) that perform internal deliberation. Suppresses "think step by step" instructions and few-shot examples, which conflict with the model's built-in chain-of-thought process.
code: public bool AvoidChainOfThought { get; init; }

name: AddOutputSchema
summary: Append an expected output schema block to the context. Reduces format drift by ~60% on Qwen models.
code: public bool AddOutputSchema { get; init; }

name: AddSelfCheck
summary: Append a self-check instruction ("verify each claim against the context above"). Catches ~1 in 3 hallucinated specifics on Qwen models.
code: public bool AddSelfCheck { get; init; }

name: ShortFocusedPrompts
summary: Prefer short, focused system prompts and lean context bodies. Enabled for Mistral and Claude Haiku.
code: public bool ShortFocusedPrompts { get; init; }

name: ContextTokenBudget
summary: Advisory token budget for the total context block. CallerDetectionService trims content to stay under this limit. Uses chars/4 estimation — see TokenEstimator.
code: public int ContextTokenBudget { get; init; } = 60_000;

name: OrderForPromptCache
summary: True for Anthropic models that benefit from putting stable content (project summary, file list) first so the prefix is cache-eligible.
code: public bool OrderForPromptCache { get; init; }

name: WillAskForMissingContext
summary: True when the consuming agent will proactively re-read files if it decides it needs more detail (Claude Code, Cursor). False means anything not sent in the MCP response is effectively invisible — summaries must be labelled and the caller should be offered full file content instead. Defaults to true (safe — only opt-out explicitly for agents that won't ask).
code: public bool WillAskForMissingContext { get; init; } = true;

name: PerFileTokenLimit
summary: Hard per-file token cap imposed by the consuming agent before it errors or silently truncates. 0 = no enforced limit (rely on ContextTokenBudget only). Continue.dev: ~10 000. Copilot: ~8 000 (silent priority-drop above this).
code: public int PerFileTokenLimit { get; init; }

name: WithClientOverrides
summary: Returns a new ContextFormat that starts from this instance (the model format) and overlays the client-application-specific properties from clientFormat. Client properties: WillAskForMissingContext, PerFileTokenLimit. All other properties (XML tags, system-prompt support, CoT, token budget, etc.) are taken from the model format (`this`).

name: MergePerFileTokenLimit
summary: Merges the model's and the client application's PerFileTokenLimit: 0 means "no limit imposed" for either side, and when both impose a limit, the stricter (lower) one wins.

name: AgentAdapterRegistry
summary: Holds all registered IAgentAdapter instances and resolves the best one for a given CallerInfo. Adapters are evaluated in descending Priority order. The first adapter whose CanHandle returns true wins. If no adapter matches, DefaultAdapter is returned.

name: Resolve
summary: Returns the highest-priority adapter that can handle caller, or the built-in DefaultAgentAdapter when nothing matches. Prefers model adapters; use ResolveBoth to get both simultaneously.

name: CallerDetectionService
summary: Detects the calling AI client and model on every MCP tool invocation. Waterfall (first non-empty match wins): 1. mcpClientName / mcpClientVersion (from IMcpServer.ClientInfo, passed in by caller) 2. X-Model-Hint header (explicit client-set model name) 3. X-LLM-Model header (alias) 4. User-Agent header (last-resort string match) 5. OllamaModel from config (when our own Ollama stack is caller) 6. Safe-default empty CallerInfo

name: ContextPartParser
summary:
Splits raw concise context (as joined by LocalContextService) into its named sections. Raw context structure — parts joined with "

": [optional] "Summary:
{text}" [optional] "Requested files: {csv}" [0-5] recent history strings [1] the user prompt (last element) Shared by every TokenSaver.AgentHelpers.* context formatter (Anthropic, Qwen, DeepSeek, OpenSource) — this parsing logic was previously duplicated verbatim across all four.

name: ParsedContextParts
summary: Result of Split — see that method for field semantics.

name: DefaultAgentAdapter
summary: Fallback adapter used when no specific adapter matches the caller. Returns the safe-default ContextFormat and passes context through unchanged.

name: TokenEstimator
summary: Fast, dependency-free token count estimator using the chars/4 heuristic. Accuracy: ±10–15% vs actual BPE tokenisers, which is acceptable for context-budget trimming. We are not billing — we are preventing context-window overflow.

name: Estimate
summary: Estimates the number of tokens in text. Returns 0 for null or empty input.

name: FitsInBudget
summary: Returns true if text fits within tokenBudget.

name: TrimToBudget
summary: Trims text to approximately tokenBudget tokens by truncating at the nearest newline boundary below the limit. Appends a trim notice if truncation occurred.

name: DeepSeekAgentAdapter
summary: Adapts concise context for DeepSeek Coder, R1, and V3 model lines. Detection: matches when the model hint contains "deepseek". Formatting strategy varies sharply by variant: R1 — reasoning model: • System prompt set to empty string (non-empty prompts degrade R1 performance) • Entire context prepended to the user message body • No chain-of-thought instructions, no few-shot examples • Minimal, direct formatting — no decorative structure V3 — chat model: • Short role statement in system prompt • XML-wrapped sections in body (workspace, files, instructions) • Markdown headers within sections for readability Coder — code-focused: • Like V3 but each file block annotated with language + path • Fenced code blocks with explicit language identifiers

name: DeepSeekContextFormatter
summary: Formats raw concise context for DeepSeek models. R1 output — everything in one flat user-message block, no system prompt: [CONTEXT] {summary if present} Requested files: {csv} {history entries} [/CONTEXT] {prompt — direct, no preamble} V3 / Coder output — structured with XML sections and Markdown headers: System prompt: "You are a helpful coding assistant. …" ## Summary {summary} ## Files {file list} {entries} {prompt} Coder additionally annotates each path reference with a fenced-code hint.

name: AnnotateFilePaths
summary: Finds patterns that look like file paths (e.g. "src/Foo.cs", "path/to/bar.ts") inside code blocks and ensures they have a language-annotated fence. Also wraps bare path mentions in the workspace/history sections with a short inline label so DeepSeek Coder can resolve them more reliably.

name: DeepSeekVariant
summary: Distinguishes the three DeepSeek model lines, each with fundamentally different prompting requirements.

name: ContinueClientAdapter
summary: Adapts context for Continue.dev (VS Code / JetBrains extension). Detection: `ClientName` matches "continue" from the MCP initialize handshake. Key behaviour differences: - Continue errors when a file context provider returns content above ~12 K tokens (~400 lines). PerFileTokenLimit is set to 10 K to stay safely below this threshold. - Continue will NOT ask for missing content if a file was truncated; it treats the received content as complete. - Underlying model varies (user-configured); we use a safe, generic Markdown format.

name: CopilotClientAdapter
summary: Adapts context for GitHub Copilot (VS Code / Copilot Chat / Copilot CLI). Detection: `ClientName` matches "copilot", "github-copilot", "vscode-copilot", or "github.copilot" from the MCP initialize handshake. Key behaviour differences from generic agents: - Copilot silently drops content above ~8 K tokens per tool response by relevance priority — it does NOT ask for missing content. - Reserves ~30–35 % of its context window as output buffer; effective context is ~130 K on a 192 K window but only ~25 K reaches us via an MCP response cap. - Always label summaries explicitly; never send a partial file without a [SUMMARY — N lines] header.

name: CursorClientAdapter
summary: Adapts context for Cursor IDE. Detection: `ClientName` matches "cursor" from the MCP initialize handshake. Key behaviour differences: - Cursor WILL re-read files independently, writing large tool output to temp files and seeking selectively. WillAskForMissingContext = true. - After its context window fills, Cursor does a lossy summarisation pass — crucial details can be lost. Prefer fewer, complete files over many shallow summaries. - Cursor only has access to a file outline + small cursor-region for large files; always include full content for files the user is actively editing. - Underlying model varies; use Markdown headers (works universally).

name: OpenSourceAgentAdapter
summary:
Adapts concise context for Llama 3, Mistral / Mixtral, and Gemma model families. Detection: matches when the model hint contains "llama", "mistral", "mixtral", or "gemma". Formatting strategy by variant: Llama: - Single system message with 2–3 sentence role framing - Markdown ## headers for context sections in the user turn - Conservative 32K token budget Mistral: - One-sentence system prompt (more = worse for Mistral) - Bullet-point lists inside context sections (improves instruction-following) - Same conservative 32K budget Gemma: - No system message (SupportsSystemPrompt = false) - System role text prepended to the first user turn, separated by "---" - Format: "You are a coding assistant.
---
## Workspace
…

{prompt}"

name: OpenSourceContextFormatter
summary: Formats raw concise context for Llama, Mistral, and Gemma models. Llama output: System prompt (2–3 sentences): "You are an expert software engineering assistant. …" User turn: ## Workspace Summary {summary} ## Requested Files {file list} ## Conversation History {history} ## Task {prompt} Mistral output: System prompt (1 sentence): "You are an expert coding assistant." User turn — same sections but rendered as bullet lists instead of prose: ## Workspace Summary - {bullet per sentence} ## Requested Files - file1.cs - file2.md ## History {entries} ## Task {prompt} Gemma output (no system message — folded into user turn): You are an expert coding assistant. --- ## Workspace Summary {summary} ## Requested Files {files} ## Task {prompt}

name: Bulletize
summary: Converts a prose paragraph into a Markdown bullet list by splitting on sentence-ending punctuation. Falls back to the original text for very short inputs or inputs that are already bullet lists.

name: OpenSourceVariant
summary: Distinguishes the three open-source model families covered by this adapter. Each has meaningfully different chat-template conventions and prompting preferences.

name: QwenAgentAdapter
summary: Adapts concise context for the Qwen 2.5 and Qwen 3.x model families. Detection: matches when the model hint contains "qwen" or "qwq". Formatting strategy: - Markdown ## headers for section separation - Role-priming sentence at the top of the system prompt - Output schema block appended (reduces format drift ~60%) - Self-check instruction appended (catches ~1 in 3 hallucinations) - Chain-of-thought instructions suppressed for Qwen3/thinking variants (they deliberate internally; external CoT prompts conflict)

name: QwenContextFormatter
summary: Formats raw concise context for Qwen models using Markdown section headers. Output structure: {role-priming line} ## Workspace Summary — if present {summary} ## Requested Files — if present {file list} ## Conversation History — if present {history entries, separated by ---} ## Current Request {prompt} ## Expected Output — always (AddOutputSchema) {output type hint} ## Verification — always (AddSelfCheck) {self-check instruction} Chain-of-thought instructions are omitted for Qwen3 and Qwen3Thinking variants.

name: OutputSchemaHint
summary: Infers the most likely output type from the prompt text to seed the output schema hint. Falls back to a general "code | explanation | plan | analysis" menu.

name: QwenVariant
summary: Distinguishes Qwen model generations and capabilities. Variant affects token budget, whether CoT instructions are suppressed, and whether a default system-prompt identity line is prepended.

name: CapabilityAssessor
summary: Answers "can CodeHelper handle this?" for a given task, language, and plan confidence. Score = 35% task-kind weight + 30% language weight + 25% plan confidence − 10% complexity penalty.

name: CodeWorkflowService
summary: Orchestrates the collaborative skeleton workflow: 1. Detect code-build intent in the prompt. 2. Build a plan and assess capability. 3. Ask the calling AI for a skeleton design. 4. Implement CanDo steps; hand off the rest back to the AI.

name: DetectCodeBuildIntent
summary: Fast keyword scan — no model call. Returns true when the prompt looks like a "please build/create code" request rather than a question, explanation request, or debugging task.

name: StartWorkflowAsync
summary: Builds a plan, assesses capability, stores a session, and returns it. The caller surfaces SkeletonRequestPrompt to the calling AI.

name: ContinueWorkflowAsync
summary: Receives the AI's skeleton design, executes CanDo plan steps, and returns a result containing applied patches and deferred steps.

name: CountSymbolsAsync
summary: Sums indexed symbol counts across the given (distinct, non-null) file paths — the real complexity signal for CapabilityAssessor. Unindexed files contribute 0, not an error, so brand-new files don't artificially spike the complexity penalty.

name: DraftModelInterceptorService
summary: Intercepts code-writing prompts and routes them through the draft model first. The draft model classifies each request as one of: - CODE: simple coding task the draft model can implement directly - ARCHITECTURE: needs design/architecture decisions from the calling AI - UNCERTAIN: draft model not confident enough, should fall back to calling AI For CODE tasks, the draft model generates the implementation, which is then applied via PatchEngine. ARCHITECTURE and UNCERTAIN tasks are deferred back to the calling AI with a structured prompt explaining what guidance is needed. This service is called from `ContextInterceptMiddleware` alongside the context cleaning pipeline.

name: TryInterceptAsync
summary: Attempts to intercept a code-writing prompt. Returns DraftModelInterceptionResult indicating whether the draft model handled it, deferred it back to the calling AI, or should be passed through as a normal tool call.

name: ImplementWithGuidanceAsync
summary: After the calling AI provides architecture guidance, use the draft model to implement the code.

name: DraftModelInterceptionResult
summary: Indicates how the draft model interceptor handled a code-writing request.

name: PassThrough
summary: Singleton: task should pass through as a normal tool call.
code: public static readonly DraftModelInterceptionResult PassThrough = new() { IsPassThrough = true };

name: HandledByDraftModel
summary: True when the draft model successfully implemented the task.
code: public bool HandledByDraftModel { get; private init; }

name: IsDeferred
summary: True when the task should be deferred back to the calling AI.
code: public bool IsDeferred { get; private init; }

name: IsPassThrough
summary: True when the task should pass through as a normal tool call.
code: public bool IsPassThrough { get; private init; }

name: NeedsArchitectureHelp
summary: True when the deferred task needs architecture/design input from the AI.
code: public bool NeedsArchitectureHelp { get; private init; }

name: Summary
summary: Summary of what was implemented or why it was deferred.
code: public string? Summary { get; private init; }

name: AppliedPatches
summary: List of applied patch results when the draft model handled it.
code: public IReadOnlyList<PatchResult> AppliedPatches { get; private init; } = [];

name: Deferred
summary: Creates a deferred result with a summary message.

name: Implemented
summary: Creates a result indicating the draft model handled the task.

name: DraftClassification
summary: Draft model's classification of a user request.

name: Language
summary: Primary file extension detected from plan path hints (e.g. ".cs").
code: public string Language { get; init; } = ".cs";

name: WorkflowSessionStore
summary: In-memory store for active workflow sessions (same pattern as PlanStore).

name: GetAll
summary: Returns all sessions, optionally filtering to those older than the given minutes.

name: CalibrationService
summary: Loads, merges, and updates calibration weights from three sources (priority order): 1. Embedded baseline JSON (lowest priority) 2. User-level file (~AppData/TokenSaver/calibration.json) 3. Workspace-level file (.local-mcp/calibration.json) ← highest priority Outcomes are appended to .local-mcp/calibration-outcomes.jsonl for auditability. Only the workspace-level file is ever written back at runtime.

name: SetAutoEnabled
summary: Persists the AutoEnabled flag to disk so the toggle survives process restarts. scope="workspace" writes AutoEnabled into the workspace-level calibration file (requires workspaceRoot); scope="global" writes it into the user-level file.

name: GetWeights
summary: Returns the merged calibration weights for the given workspace root.

name: RecordOutcome
summary: Records a post-review outcome and adjusts workspace-level weights accordingly. Never touches the user-level file.

name: GetStats
summary: Returns calibration stats for the MCP diagnostics tool.

name: ResolveAutoEnabled
summary: Resolves the effective AutoEnabled flag: persisted workspace override, then persisted user-level override, then the config-file/in-memory default passed in.

name: AutoEnabled
summary: Enable auto-workflow intercept for code-build prompts. Opt-in; defaults off.
code: public bool AutoEnabled { get; set; }

name: SkeletonTimeoutSec
summary: Seconds to wait for the calling AI to return a skeleton before timing out.
code: public int SkeletonTimeoutSec { get; set; } = 60;

name: CanDoThreshold
summary: Composite score at or above which CodeHelper claims full ownership of a step.
code: public double CanDoThreshold { get; set; } = 0.70;

name: DeferThreshold
summary: Composite score below which CodeHelper defers the step entirely to the AI.
code: public double DeferThreshold { get; set; } = 0.40;

name: WasteThreshold
summary: Fraction of work the AI had to redo before the scaffold counts as "not worth it". If correctionRatio >= WasteThreshold, calibration weights are decremented.
code: public double WasteThreshold { get; set; } = 0.40;

name: LearningRate
summary: Step size for weight updates each time an outcome is recorded (0.0–1.0).
code: public double LearningRate { get; set; } = 0.10;

name: UserCalibrationPath
summary: Absolute path to the user-level calibration file. Empty = platform default.
code: public string UserCalibrationPath { get; set; } = "";

name: WorkspaceCalibrationPath
summary: Workspace-relative path to the workspace-level calibration file.
code: public string WorkspaceCalibrationPath { get; set; } = ".tokensaver/calibration.json";

name: TaskKindCalibrationPolicy
summary: Per-task-kind calibration policy overrides. Key = PlanTaskKind.ToString(). Tasks not listed use LearningRateMultiplier=1.0 and MinSamplesBeforeAdjust=1.
code: public Dictionary<string, TaskKindCalibrationPolicy> TaskKindPolicies { get; set; } = new()

name: AiSummarizationService
summary: Produces a per-file description: AI summary (when a summarizer is configured and the extension is a supported source-code type) with a static-extraction fallback.

name: CodeParserUtils
summary: Shared utilities used by all symbol parsers and WorkspaceCodeScanner.

name: ExtractBraceBlock
summary: Starting at startIndex (on or just before the opening '{'), finds the matching closing '}' and returns the content between braces. Returns null if the block exceeds maxChars or is not found.

name: ExtractXmlSummary
summary: Extracts the first line of an XML `` doc comment immediately preceding the given position in the source. Returns null if none found within the previous 8 lines.

name: MakeId
summary: Stable, non-cryptographic id from file path + symbol name + line number. Not used for security purposes — only for deterministic symbol identity in the index. Uses SHA-256 (truncated) purely because it's a convenient, collision-resistant, built-in stable hash; no cryptographic guarantee is required or relied upon here.

name: ContextPipelineService
summary: Context-building pipeline (replaces LocalContextService): concise-context assembly, hygiene reporting, and on-demand file content retrieval. Depends on the WorkspaceIndexService orchestrator for indexing side effects (IndexWorkspaceAsync / EnsureFileIndexedAsync) triggered as part of building context. This is a one-way dependency — the orchestrator's own kept methods (IndexWorkspaceAsync, IndexFileAsync, EnsureFileIndexedAsync, IndexOneFileAsync) never call back into this service, so there's no DI constructor cycle.

name: CSharpSymbolParser
summary: Regex-based C# symbol parser. Handles types (class/interface/struct/enum/record/delegate) and members (methods, constructors, properties, fields, events). No Roslyn dependency — works on any text without SDK/build context.

name: DependencyTrackingService
summary: Cross-file symbol dependency queries, backed by SymbolReferences.

name: GetFileDependenciesAsync
summary: NOTE: SymbolReferences is currently never populated by any ISymbolParser (same limitation as the old code-index.db `references_` table it replaces) — this will return an empty list until a parser starts emitting cross-file symbol edges.

name: GetFileDependentsAsync
summary: See GetFileDependenciesAsync note — currently always empty.

name: FolderTreeManager
summary: Owns the Folder tree: bootstrap creation, incremental ancestor-chain creation for single-file updates, description aggregation, and on-demand folder-index JSON retrieval (replaces the old LocalContextService folder_indices JSON blob).

name: EnsureFolderChainAsync
summary: Ensures the ancestor chain root..folderRel exists, creating only what's missing. Cheap for incremental single-file updates (proportional to path depth, not tree size).

name: RefreshTouchedFolderDescriptionsAsync
summary: Regenerates the Description for every folder touched by this index pass, plus all their ancestors up to the root, from a cheap static aggregate of immediate children (no extra AI calls — file-level descriptions already carry the detail).

name: GenericSymbolParser
summary: Fallback symbol parser for Python, Go, Java, and other languages. Uses simple, broadly-applicable patterns.

name: GitStalenessService
summary: Git-aware staleness resolution (§2 of the design doc): figures out which workspace-relative files need reindexing without a full filesystem walk when a git baseline exists, and reports files whose on-disk mtime has moved past what's indexed.

name: ResolveTargetFilesAsync
summary: Returns the exact workspace-relative files that need reindexing, or null if there's no git anywhere under the workspace (caller should do a full walk — mtime is the only signal available, and IndexOneFileAsync's own LastModified check handles that per-file).

name: EnumerateAllFiles
summary: Full-tree walk honoring .gitignore/context-exclusions/AlwaysSkipDirs. Shared with the orchestrator's bootstrap indexing path (see WorkspaceIndexService.IndexWorkspaceAsync).

name: IFileReindexer
summary: Minimal seam for re-indexing a single file after it is written. Lets consumers like `PatchEngine` depend on just the re-index call rather than the full WorkspaceIndexService, which keeps them testable without the heavy indexing dependency graph.

name: SymbolSearchService
summary: Symbol graph queries (replaces CodeIndexService): exact-name lookup, per-file symbol counts, and free-text search over indexed Symbol rows.

name: CountSymbolsInFileAsync
summary: Returns the number of indexed symbols (functions/types) in a single file, used as the real complexity signal for CapabilityAssessor instead of a step-count proxy. Returns 0 if the file has not been indexed yet.

name: TypeScriptSymbolParser
summary: Regex-based TypeScript/JavaScript symbol parser. Handles class, interface, type alias, and function/arrow-function declarations.

name: WorkspaceCodeScanner
summary: Scans workspace source files and generates TestCase objects that exercise the local model on real code from the project. Supported languages: C# (.cs), TypeScript (.ts) Test categories generated: completion, review, docstring

name: WorkspaceConfigManager
summary: Workspace root/path resolution and the plain-JSON preferences file (.tokensaver/preferences.json) — unrelated to the indexing schema.

name: WorkspaceIndexDbAccessor
summary: Shared DB-access seam for the split WorkspaceIndexService: owns the single cached WorkspaceIndexContext plus the lock that serializes all access to it (EF Core's DbContext isn't thread-safe). Every other extracted indexing service depends on this and calls GetDbAsync; DB reads/writes go through WithDbLockAsync{T}(Func{Task{T}},CancellationToken) (or the void overload) instead of touching a raw semaphore field directly.

name: WithDbLockAsync
summary: Runs action while holding the DB lock, returning its result. Preferred wrapper for all DB reads/writes instead of acquiring the raw semaphore directly — keeps lock acquire/release symmetric across every extracted service.

name: WithDbLockAsync

name: WorkspaceIndexService
summary: Unified replacement for the old LocalContextService (context.db: files/sections/summaries/ folder_indices JSON) and CodeIndexService (code-index.db: file_manifest/symbols/references_). Every file not excluded by .gitignore/ExcludePatterns/context-exclusions gets a File row (type + description); files matching an ISymbolParser additionally get Symbol rows. Staleness is git-aware (see GitStalenessChecker) with a per-file last-write-time fallback for non-git folders. See plans/TokenSaver.UnifiedIndex.plan.md. Slimmed orchestrator: owns only the indexing pipeline itself (bootstrap/incremental index, pruning, single-file re-index) and delegates everything else — DB access, staleness resolution, folder tree maintenance, symbol queries, AI summarization, context building, dependency queries, and workspace config/preferences — to the extracted services below.

Cheap to call on every BuildConciseContext request: when nothing changed, this is just one or two `git` subprocess calls per repo root.

name: Task
summary: Sweeps every indexed FileEntity row and removes ones that no longer belong in the index: files deleted from disk, and files now covered by .gitignore or context-exclusions (e.g. a pattern added after the file was originally indexed). Symbol rows are removed via the FK cascade (see WorkspaceIndexContext.OnModelCreating) — the explicit Symbols delete here exists only to report an accurate pruned-symbol count, since ExecuteDeleteAsync on Files wouldn't tell us how many child rows cascaded. Folders are intentionally left alone: an empty folder is still valid structure, and the folder-description refresh already reports "no files" / "empty folder" for it.

name: LogStrippingStage
summary: Stage 2 — Log Stripping. Collapses log blocks (>3 consecutive log lines) to: omission placeholder + extracted ERROR/EXCEPTION lines + last N lines verbatim.

name: CodeBlockCollapsingStage
summary: Stage 3 — Code Block Collapsing. Replaces fenced code blocks over the configured line threshold with a compact reference. Full content is stored in `PipelineContext.CollapsedBlocks` for later retrieval. Weight-aware: if CodeWeight ≥ 0.8 the threshold is raised by 30 lines.

name: ConversationSummarizationStage

name: ToolCallCompressionStage

name: SemanticRelevanceFilterStage

Key files from PromptAssessment always get a minimum floor of 0.5. Degrades gracefully if the embedding endpoint is unavailable.

name: TokenBudgetStage
summary: Stage 7 — Token Budget Enforcement. Trims context to fit within the configured budget (with safety margin). Drop order: lowest-relevance chunks first, then summarize oldest non-verbatim chunks.

name: ChunkingStage
summary: Stage 8 — Chunking (runs before Stage 6 in actual pipeline order). Splits history turns and query into semantic ContextChunks. Each chunk is labelled with source, kind, section name, and token count.

name: ConversationalGarbageStage

name: FormattingNormalizationStage

name: AiProviderConfigService

That approach is removed: writing MCP client configuration files programmatically proved unreliable across providers — different tools use different file formats and root keys, some are JSONC with comments/trailing commas, and concurrent edits by the user's editor could race with an automated writer and clobber each other's changes. Auto-detection/auto-write is now a no-op. Use the "TokenSaver: Open Install Prompt" VS Code command instead, which opens `INSTALL_PROMPT.md` — copy-paste instructions (for httpStreaming or stdio transport) that an AI agent or the user can follow to wire up any of these providers manually, with full context and verification. Note: Claude Desktop / Cowork (claude_desktop_config.json) was never handled here — that one-time registration still happens via the installer script (setup.ps1).

Detection/auto-write is removed for all providers — always returns an empty list now. See the class doc comment and INSTALL_PROMPT.md for the manual-install flow that replaces this.

name: UpdateAllProvidersAsync

Since DetectProviders now always returns an empty list, this returns an empty result list — kept only so existing callers (the `/api/register-providers` endpoint, `RegisterMcpProviders` MCP tool) don't need to change their call sites. See INSTALL_PROMPT.md for the manual-install flow.

name: UpdateProviderAsync

name: ChunkExtractor
summary: Default IChunkExtractor — see that interface's doc comment for scope/rationale.

name: DraftModelCapacityClient
summary: Queries DraftModel.Loader's `GET /api/capacity` endpoint so background indexing (AI file/folder summaries) can size its concurrency off this machine's real capacity instead of guessing from CPU count. summary: Loads the .gitignore at workspaceRoot. Returns an empty (pass-all) filter if the file doesn't exist.

name: IsIgnored
summary: Returns true if the path should be excluded. relativePath must use forward slashes and must NOT start with '/'. isDirectory must be true when the path refers to a directory.

name: EntryIsCovered
summary: Returns true if entry (a workspace-relative path such as ".tokensaver" or ".local-mcp/indices") is already covered by a rule in the workspace .gitignore. Handles parent-directory rules: ".local-mcp/" covers ".local-mcp/indices".

name: AddEntries
summary: Appends one or more entries to the workspace .gitignore (creating the file if needed). Each entry is written as a directory glob ("entry/") unless IsFile is true. A shared header comment is written before the block.

name: GitignoreIssue
summary: Describes a workspace path that exists but is not covered by .gitignore.

name: GitignoreScanner
summary: Scans a workspace and reports paths that exist on disk but are not covered by .gitignore. Only paths that actually exist are reported — the scanner does not produce noise for toolchains that aren't in use.

name: IsKnownEntry
summary: Returns true if name is already tracked by this scanner.

name: Scan
summary: Returns a list of GitignoreIssue for paths that actually exist in workspaceRoot but are not covered by the workspace .gitignore.

name: RepoStalenessResult
summary: Result of a staleness check for one repo root. IsFirstRun and Unchanged are mutually exclusive with a non-empty ChangedFiles: first run or "git unavailable" → caller should do a full scan under this repo root; unchanged → skip entirely; otherwise → only re-index ChangedFiles.

name: GitStalenessChecker
summary: Detects which files changed since the last index run using git as the staleness source of truth (HEAD sha + working-tree dirty state) instead of walking and hashing every file on every startup. Falls back to IsFirstRun semantics when git isn't available or the folder isn't a repo — callers should then fall back to comparing each tracked file's last-write-time against its stored value.

name: DiscoverRepoRoots
summary: Finds every git repo root under the workspace: the workspace root itself (if it is one) plus any nested/vendored repos (monorepo submodules, etc.). Returns workspace-relative paths, "." for the workspace root.

name: CheckAsync
summary: Compares the repo's current HEAD sha + dirty state against the stored RepoStalenessEntity row, computes the exact changed-file set when something differs, and persists the new sha/dirty/CheckedAt as a side effect.

name: ParsePorcelainPaths
summary: Parses `git status --porcelain` lines: "XY path" or "XY orig -> path" for renames.

name: IPromptAdapter
summary: Adapts a raw prompt for a specific local model before sending to inference. Implementations apply model-family-specific structuring: role-priming, output schema hints, self-check instructions, and token budget trimming. The interface lives in `TokenSaver.Library` so low-level services (OllamaService, PlanBuilder, etc.) can depend on it without pulling in `TokenSaver.AgentHelpers.Core`. The concrete implementation is registered in `TokenSaver.MCP` backed by `AgentAdapterRegistry`.

name: ModelRouteResolver
summary: Resolves a task_type string (e.g. "code", "chat", "summarize", "embed", "rerank") to an Ollama model name via TokenEconomyConfig.ModelRoutes — centralizes model choice in one place instead of hardcoding a model name per tool/service. Backs the ModelRoute MCP tool and is used internally by DistillationService/RepoIndexer.

name: Resolve
summary: Returns the configured model for taskType, falling back to the "chat" route, then to OllamaModel/EffectiveModel if even "chat" isn't configured (should not happen with TokenEconomyConfig's defaults, but keeps this resolver total rather than throwing on a misconfigured route table).

name: OllamaCodeSummarizer
summary: Implements ICodeSummarizer by calling the configured Ollama model (uses EffectiveModel — typically the draft/helper model) with a short summarisation prompt. Results are NOT cached here; caching is handled by the caller (LocalContextService) via the SQLite `summaries` table so the cache survives server restarts and is keyed on content hash rather than file path. The prompt intentionally avoids chain-of-thought framing and asks for a single sentence. This keeps latency low (the draft model is fast) and the output dense enough to fit comfortably in an index JSON `explanation` field.

name: FindBackupEndpointName
summary: Picks a healthy, non-primary configured endpoint by name for background indexing to use, so bulk summarization doesn't compete with interactive requests for the primary endpoint's capacity. Returns null (meaning "use normal selection") when only a single endpoint is configured/synthesized, or when no non-primary endpoint is currently healthy.

name: OllamaEndpointStatus
summary: Runtime health/usage snapshot for one configured Ollama endpoint. Reset on process restart — no persistence, matching the plan's "no historical persistence required" note.

name: NextRetryAt
summary: When set and in the future, this endpoint is in an exponential-backoff window and will be skipped by automatic selection until this time, even if marked unhealthy.
code: public DateTimeOffset? NextRetryAt { get; init; }

name: OllamaEndpointRegistry
summary: Tracks configured Ollama endpoints and their runtime health, and selects which endpoint a given call should use according to EndpointSelectStrategy. When Endpoints is empty (the default — most installs), this registry synthesizes a single endpoint named "default" from the flat OllamaUrl/OllamaModel settings, so single-endpoint behavior is preserved with zero config changes.

name: BaseBackoffDelay
summary: Initial backoff delay applied after the first consecutive failure.

name: MaxBackoffDelay
summary: Ceiling for the exponential backoff delay, regardless of consecutive-failure count.

name: SelectEndpoint
summary: Selects an endpoint URL to use for the next call.

name: IsEligibleNow
summary: True when the endpoint has no active backoff window, or its window has elapsed.

name: ComputeBackoffDelay
summary: Computes the exponential backoff delay for the given consecutive-failure count: BaseBackoffDelay * 2^(failures-1), capped at MaxBackoffDelay. Failure count 0 or less yields TimeSpan.Zero (no backoff).

name: SetHealth
summary: Used by `EndpointHealthMonitor` to record probe outcomes without a call.

name: ConsecutiveFailures
summary: Consecutive failures since the last success, used to size the backoff delay.

name: NextRetryAt
summary: Earliest time this endpoint may be selected/probed again after a failure. Null when eligible now.

name: OllamaRequestOptions
summary: Key used on Options to request a specific Ollama endpoint by name for a single call. Read by `TokenSaver.MCP.Services.EndpointRoutingHandler`. Declared here (rather than in the MCP project) so library-level callers like OllamaService can set it without a back-reference to TokenSaver.MCP.

name: CallModelAsync
summary: Calls the local model with a single prompt. The prompt is run through the registered IPromptAdapter (if any) before sending.

name: CallModelOnEndpointAsync
summary: Calls the local model with a single prompt, optionally pinned to a specific configured endpoint (see Endpoints). Passing null uses the registry's normal selection strategy.

name: CallModelAsync
summary: Calls the local model with an explicit model name and prompt.

name: CallModelAsync
summary: Calls the local model with a separate system prompt and user prompt. The userPrompt is adapted via IPromptAdapter if registered; the systemPrompt is sent as-is (already well-structured by the caller).

name: CallModelAsync
summary: Calls the local model with a separate system prompt and user prompt, optionally pinned to a specific configured endpoint. The userPrompt is adapted via IPromptAdapter if registered; the systemPrompt is sent as-is.

name: EmbedAsync
summary: Generates an embedding vector for input via Ollama's `POST /api/embeddings` endpoint (not to be confused with `/api/generate` used by CallModelAsync(string,string,CancellationToken)). Requires an embedding-capable model to be pulled locally (e.g. `nomic-embed-text`) — a chat model like the configured EffectiveModel will not work here.

name: WaitForReadyAsync
summary: Polls until the Ollama router is reachable and has at least one model available, or until timeout elapses. Returns true if ready, false if timed out.

name: RawArtifactWriter
summary: Escape hatch for distilling tools: writes raw output to "/.tokensaver/raw//.txt" before distillation, so a compressed summary is never a dead end — Claude (or the user) can read the full raw artifact by path if the summary isn't enough. Gated by TokenEconomyConfig.EnableRawRetention; WriteAsync returns null (skips the write) when disabled, and callers should omit the "full: " reference from their response text in that case rather than reference a path that was never written.

name: RepoIndexer
summary: Default IRepoIndexer — see that interface's doc comment.

name: SavingsTracker
summary: EF Core/SQLite-backed ISavingsTracker, storing rows in the shared ".tokensaver/index.db" via TokenEconomyDbAccessor — see that type's doc comment for why this doesn't reuse TokenSaver.CodeHelper's WorkspaceIndexDbAccessor.

name: SemanticSearchService
summary: Default ISemanticSearchService — see that interface's doc comment.

name: StaticFileSummarizer
summary: Extracts a short human-readable description of a file from its content without calling any AI model — used as the fallback (or the only source, for extensions the summarizer doesn't cover) when building each File row's Description. Ported unchanged from the old LocalContextService.ExtractStaticSummaryAsync.

name: IsProbablyBinary
summary: Cheap binary sniff: a NUL byte in the first 4KB is a strong binary signal. Used so "index every file" doesn't try to line-split images/executables as text.

name: SuspiciousDirRecommendation
summary: How the path should be handled if the user agrees it is generated/cached.

name: SuspiciousDirectory
summary: A workspace directory that looks like a cache or build artefact but wasn't positively identified.

name: SuspiciousDirectoryScanner
summary: Scans a workspace for directories that look like caches or build outputs but are not covered by the known-good list in GitignoreScanner (for workspace-root entries) or by .gitignore. Two complementary passes are used: Heuristic pass — name patterns and content sampling, up to `maxDepth` levels deep. Deep build-artifact pass — targeted BFS for known build output names (`bin`, `obj`, etc.) at any depth; uses the fixed gitignore pattern rules to determine coverage.

name: HighConfidenceNames
summary: Exact directory names that are highly likely to be caches/build output.

name: MediumConfidenceNames
summary: Names that are well-known build outputs but could also be intentional source dirs — flagged at medium confidence.

name: CacheSubstrings
summary: Substrings in a directory name that suggest it is a cache.

name: CompiledExtensions
summary: File extensions that dominate generated / compiled output directories. A directory where >80% of sampled files have these extensions is suspicious.

name: DeepBuildNames
summary: Names targeted in the deep BFS pass; these appear at arbitrary nesting depth in multi-project repos. The workspace-root occurrence is already handled by GitignoreScanner, so we only report nested occurrences here.

name: Scan
summary: Scans workspaceRoot and returns directories that look like caches/build outputs but are not covered by .gitignore.

name: ChunkExtractorTests
summary: Covers IChunkExtractor's regex-boundary heuristics directly — pure string-in/chunks-out, no Ollama/DB dependency, so every case here is fast and fully deterministic.

name: DistillationServiceTests
summary: Covers DistillationService's kill-switch/raw-fallback path, which is the one path guaranteed to never call out to a real Ollama process — every other path (actual compression) needs a live model and is out of scope for this unit-test-only suite, same as OllamaEndpointRegistryTests' documented split between offline-testable and live-verification behavior.

name: OllamaEndpointRegistryTests
summary: Covers the plan's "Testing" section items that don't require a live Ollama process: failover when primary is down, round-robin distribution, explicit selection against an offline/unknown endpoint, and the exponential-backoff behavior added on top of the original health-tracking implementation. Health-monitor recovery detection and latency-comparison items remain manual/live-verification steps (see plan status notes) — they require a real HTTP endpoint to probe.

name: SavingsTrackerTests
summary: Verdict() is pure logic (no I/O) and covered directly. RecordAsync/GetReportAsync/ GetOneAsync open a real SQLite file under a fresh temp directory per test — cheap and fully deterministic, no Ollama dependency (SavingsTracker never calls Ollama itself).

name: TokenEconomyDbAccessor
summary: DB-access seam for the token-economy services (SavingsTracker, RepoIndexer, SemanticSearchService) — owns a single cached WorkspaceIndexContext per workspace root plus the lock that serializes access to it (EF Core's DbContext isn't thread-safe), mirroring `TokenSaver.CodeHelper.Indexing.WorkspaceIndexDbAccessor`'s pattern exactly. Deliberately a separate accessor/instance rather than reusing `WorkspaceIndexDbAccessor` directly: that type lives in TokenSaver.CodeHelper, which already depends on TokenSaver.Library — depending on it from here would be a backwards/ circular project reference. Both accessors open the same underlying SQLite file (".tokensaver/index.db", the one DB file for this workspace) via WorkspaceIndexContextFactory; WAL mode (enabled by the factory) allows multiple connections against it safely, and this accessor's tables (Chunks, TokenSavings) don't overlap with WorkspaceIndexDbAccessor's writes (Folders/Files/Symbols) — only a read-only FK reference from Chunks to Files.

name: WithDbLockAsync
summary: Runs action while holding the DB lock, returning its result.

name: WithDbLockAsync
summary: Void-returning overload of WithDbLockAsync{T}(Func{Task{T}},CancellationToken).

name: WorkspaceIndexContext
summary: EF Core-backed replacement for the old context.db (files/sections/summaries/folder_indices, the latter a JSON blob per folder) and code-index.db (file_manifest/symbols/references_) SQLite caches. One instance per workspace, stored at ".tokensaver/index.db". See plans/TokenSaver.UnifiedIndex.plan.md for the design rationale.

name: Chunks
summary: Function/class/markdown-section chunks — see ChunkEntity. Populated by RepoIndexer, queried by SemanticGrep.
code: public DbSet<ChunkEntity> Chunks => Set<ChunkEntity>();

name: TokenSavings
summary: Per-distill()-call savings log — see TokenSavingsEntity. Populated by SavingsTracker, queried by TokenSavingsReport/WorthKeeping.
code: public DbSet<TokenSavingsEntity> TokenSavings => Set<TokenSavingsEntity>();

name: FolderOverviews
summary: Keyless entity backed by the folder_overview view. Read-only — see CreateAsync for where the view is created.
code: public DbSet<FolderOverview> FolderOverviews => Set<FolderOverview>();

name: WorkspaceIndexContextFactory
summary: Opens the unified per-workspace index database, creating the schema, enabling WAL mode, and (re)creating the folder_overview view on first open. Callers should create one context per workspace per process and reuse it (mirrors the old single-connection-per-process pattern in LocalContextService / CodeIndexService).

name: CreateAsync
summary: Opens (creating if needed) the unified workspace index for the given workspace root, ensures the schema exists, enables WAL, and (re)creates the folder_overview view.

name: ChunkEntity
summary: One row per function/class/markdown-section chunk within an indexed file — finer-grained than FileEntity's single per-file Description. Populated by RepoIndexer (TokenSaver.Library.Services.IRepoIndexer) and queried by SemanticGrep via cosine similarity over EmbeddingVector. Unlike SymbolEntity (exact/substring name search over statically-parsed symbols), this table exists specifically for natural-language semantic search, so it carries an AI-generated summary and an embedding vector rather than a parsed symbol kind.

name: RelativePath
summary: Workspace-relative file path. Deliberately NOT a foreign key into FileEntity — RepoIndexer/SemanticGrep are independently runnable from the CodeIndex/WorkspaceIndexService pipeline (no requirement that a file has been symbol-indexed before it can be chunk-indexed), so this table has no dependency on that one's lifecycle. Coincidentally overlapping rows in both tables for the same file are expected and fine.
code: public string RelativePath { get; set; } = "";

name: ChunkType
summary: "function" | "class" | "md_section" | "module" (whole-file fallback for unsupported extensions).
code: public string ChunkType { get; set; } = "";

name: Name
summary: Function/class name, or markdown heading text, or the file's base name for a "module" chunk.
code: public string Name { get; set; } = "";

name: ContentHash
summary: Hash of the chunk's own text (not the whole file) — re-summarizing/re-embedding is skipped when unchanged.
code: public string ContentHash { get; set; } = "";

name: Summary
summary: One-line AI-generated summary. This is what SemanticGrep shows Claude — not the raw chunk text.
code: public string Summary { get; set; } = "";

name: EmbeddingVector
summary: JSON-encoded float[] embedding. Embeds Summary when TokenEconomyConfig.EnableSummaryEmbedding is true (default), or the raw chunk text otherwise — see RepoIndexer.
code: public string EmbeddingVector { get; set; } = "";

name: FileEntity
summary: One row per indexed file. Absorbs both the old context.db `files`/`sections` tables (previously split: file metadata vs. minified content) and the old code-index.db `file_manifest` table — merged into a single table per the unified-index design.

name: RelativePath
summary: Workspace-relative path, unique.
code: public string RelativePath { get; set; } = "";

name: FileType
summary: Extension-derived type/language, e.g. "csharp", "markdown", "json", "binary".
code: public string FileType { get; set; } = "";

name: Description
summary: Static-extraction and/or AI-generated one-paragraph summary of contents.
code: public string Description { get; set; } = "";

name: FolderEntity
summary: One row per workspace folder. Replaces the old context.db `folder_indices` table, which stored one JSON blob per folder — normalized here so folder/file/symbol counts can be queried with real joins (see FolderOverview) instead of parsing JSON client-side.

name: RelativePath
summary: Workspace-relative path; "." for the workspace root.
code: public string RelativePath { get; set; } = "";

name: ParentFolderId
summary: Null for the workspace root folder.
code: public int? ParentFolderId { get; set; }

name: Description
summary: One-paragraph description of this folder's contents, detailed enough for the draft model to decide whether it needs to descend into it for a given request.
code: public string Description { get; set; } = "";

name: LastModified
summary: Unix ms. For folders under a git repo, staleness is primarily driven by RepoStalenessEntity instead; this is the fallback / display value.
code: public long LastModified { get; set; }

name: FolderOverview
summary: Keyless entity mapped to the `folder_overview` SQL view (created manually by WorkspaceIndexContextFactory, since EF Core's EnsureCreated does not generate DDL for entities configured with ToView). One row per folder: file/symbol counts and freshest child mtime in a single query, so "does the draft model need to descend into this folder" doesn't require walking children.

name: RepoStalenessEntity
summary: One row per git repo root detected under the workspace (the workspace root itself, plus any nested/vendored repos). Checked on first DB load per process: if HEAD sha and dirty-flag are unchanged since CheckedAt, that repo's files are skipped entirely rather than re-walked. See plans/TokenSaver.UnifiedIndex.plan.md §2.

name: RepoRootPath
summary: Workspace-relative path to the repo root; "." if the workspace root itself is the repo.
code: public string RepoRootPath { get; set; } = "";

name: LastDirty
summary: True if `git status --porcelain` was non-empty at the last check.
code: public bool LastDirty { get; set; }

name: SymbolEntity
summary: One row per function/type/section within a file. Replaces code-index.db's `symbols` table. Id keeps the existing stable-hash scheme (SHA1 of FilePath+Name+Line) from TokenSaver.CodeHelper's SymbolEntry so existing symbol ids remain valid across the swap.

name: Kind
summary: Maps to TokenSaver.CodeHelper.Models.Index.SymbolKind. Stored as int here so TokenSaver.Library doesn't need a project reference to TokenSaver.CodeHelper.
code: public int Kind { get; set; }

name: Description
summary: XML-doc summary or AI/static-inferred description.
code: public string? Description { get; set; }

name: LastModified
summary: Inherited from the parent File's LastModified at index time.
code: public long LastModified { get; set; }

name: SymbolReferenceEntity
summary: A directed edge between two symbols (e.g. "method A calls method B"). Deliberately has no EF-modeled FK relationship to SymbolEntity — during incremental reindexing a reference can transiently point at a symbol id that hasn't been re-parsed yet, same as the old code-index.db `references_` table (which also had no FK constraint).

name: TokenSavingsEntity
summary: One row per distill() call, recorded by SavingsTracker (when TokenEconomyConfig.EnableSavingsTracking is true) so TokenSavingsReport/WorthKeeping can answer "what's actually saving the most tokens" from a query instead of a guess.

name: Tool
summary: Calling tool name, e.g. "runTests", "containerLogs", "diffSummarize".
code: public string Tool { get; set; } = "";

name: Role
summary: Distill role used, e.g. "test_failure", "log_errors".
code: public string Role { get; set; } = "";

name: Terse
summary: Whether terse-mode was active for this specific call.
code: public bool Terse { get; set; }

name: SavedTokens
summary: RawTokens - DistilledTokens, stored directly so reports don't recompute it per query.
code: public int SavedTokens { get; set; }

name: DurationMs
summary: Ollama call latency for this distillation, in milliseconds.
code: public int DurationMs { get; set; }

name: MigrateLegacyDataFolder
summary: One-time migration of the per-workspace data folder from its pre-rename name (".local-helper", from when this project was "LocalHelper") to its current name (".tokensaver"). Every constant across TokenSaver.Library/TokenSaver.CodeHelper/etc. already points at ".tokensaver" — this just moves any pre-existing folder on first startup after upgrading, so an existing workspace's index/config/cache isn't silently orphaned. No-ops if the new folder already exists (migration already happened, or this is a fresh workspace) or if the legacy folder doesn't exist.

name: DraftModelHealthCheck
summary: Health check that probes the DraftModel router (via OllamaService) and reports whether it is reachable, has models available, and has models loaded in VRAM. Healthy — router reachable, ≥1 model available (VRAM state reported via data["vram_state"]; "idle" just means keep_alive expired the model, not a problem — next request reloads it, incurring a one-time cold-load delay) Unhealthy — router unreachable, or no models pulled

name: SelfTestHealthCheck
summary: Exercises a handful of the server's own lightweight, in-process code paths (no network I/O — this deliberately does not call DraftModel/Ollama; that's DraftModelHealthCheck's job) to catch a broken configuration/wiring bug before a real caller does. Mirrors DraftModel.Loader's `RunSelfTests` in RouterHttpServer: each check is independent — one throwing doesn't stop the rest — and a failure is reported as Degraded with which check failed and why, even though the process is obviously still up and responding. Deliberately untagged so it participates in `/health` but not the `"ready"`-tagged `/health/ready` predicate — this is a self-diagnostic, not a dependency-reachability check.

name: UnhandledFaultHealthCheck
summary: Reports Degraded when UnhandledFaultTracker has a recent unhandled exception on record (see FaultTrackingMiddleware), even though the process itself is clearly still up and running (it's answering this very health check). Deliberately untagged — it participates in the full `/health` report but not the `"ready"`-tagged predicate `/health/ready` uses, matching DraftModel.Loader's split between full self-diagnostic health and cheap readiness.

name: ContextInterceptMiddleware
summary: Intercepts MCP tools/call requests and runs the prompt through: 1. Context cleaning pipeline (existing) 2. Draft model interceptor (new) — for code-writing prompts, tries the local draft model first; falls back to the calling AI for architecture/design. Works for every MCP client (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Continue, etc.) because it sits at the HTTP level, not inside any single tool. Only fires when: - The request is a JSON-RPC tools/call - The tool arguments contain a "prompt" field - The tool is not one of the context tools themselves (avoid recursion) - CodeHelperConfig.AutoEnabled is true

name: FaultTrackingMiddleware
summary: Wraps every request in a try/catch that records unhandled exceptions into UnhandledFaultTracker before re-throwing, so a stack trace anywhere downstream (an MCP tool call, ContextInterceptMiddleware, the provider-registration endpoint, etc.) is visible from `/health` even though the process itself keeps running and answering requests normally otherwise. Deliberately registered as early as possible in the pipeline (see Program.cs) so it wraps every other middleware and the MCP endpoint itself — the goal is "any unhandled exception on this server", not just ones from a specific subsystem. Re-throws rather than swallowing: this middleware only adds observability. Downstream error handling (ASP.NET Core's default 500 response, or any exception-handler middleware added later) behaves exactly as it would without this middleware present.

name: AgentHelpersPromptAdapter
summary: IPromptAdapter implementation backed by AgentAdapterRegistry. Resolves the appropriate adapter for the configured local model and applies its full structuring (role-priming, output schema, self-check, token budget trimming). Registered as a singleton in `Program.cs` so OllamaService and any other consumers receive adaptation automatically.

name: DeferredNotificationService
summary: Thread-safe queue for messages and questions that background services need to surface to the user. Background services (e.g. ProviderAutoRegistrationService) have no active MCP session to reply through, so they post here instead. The next tool call that reaches an active client drains the queue and prepends the content to its response. Two kinds of items: Notification — informational (e.g. "Registered with Continue at ~/.continue/…") Question — requires a follow-up action (e.g. "Found new providers — call X to register") Use Post() for fire-and-forget info; PostQuestion() when you want the user to act.

name: Post
summary: Queues an informational message to surface on the next tool call.

name: PostQuestion
summary: Queues a question that requires user action. Include the tool call the user should make to answer in the message text.

name: Drain
summary: Removes and returns all pending items. Call from a tool handler that has an active client session so the content actually reaches the user.

name: DrainFormatted
summary: Formats drained items into a block ready to prepend to a tool response. Returns an empty string if the queue was empty.

name: DraftModelConfigResolver
summary: Resolves the effective Ollama/DraftModel router endpoint for this process, by reading DraftModel.Loader's own ProgramData config file when installed as a Windows service, and synthesizes a matching named endpoint entry so `OllamaEndpointRegistry` can select it like any other configured endpoint. Pulled out of `Program.cs` so the composition root only calls one method instead of embedding this parsing/synthesis logic inline.

name: ApplyIfInstalled
summary: If DraftModelServiceInstalled is set, reads DraftModel.Loader's ProgramData config (JSONC — comments/trailing commas allowed) and, when found, updates config.OllamaUrl to the discovered router host/port and adds a "draftmodel-loader" entry to config.Endpoints (unless already present). Any failure to read or parse the file is swallowed and the caller falls through to its already-configured OllamaUrl — this is a best-effort auto-discovery, not a hard requirement.

name: AddSynthesizedEndpointIfMissing
summary: Also expose the router as a named, selectable endpoint (e.g. via CleanAndChat's endpointName param or explicit/round-robin strategies) alongside any other endpoints configured in TokenSaver:Endpoints, rather than only ever being reachable as the flat OllamaUrl fallback. Per the plan's "DraftModel.Loader as an optional endpoint" integration point. Skipped if the user already defined an endpoint with this name.

name: EndpointHealthMonitor
summary: Background service that periodically pings every configured Ollama endpoint's `/api/tags` (a cheap, always-available Ollama route) and updates OllamaEndpointRegistry health state accordingly. Logs healthyunhealthy transitions (the registry itself logs the transition; this service just drives the polling loop). Interval is configurable via HealthCheckInterval (default 30s).

name: EndpointRoutingHandler
summary: DelegatingHandler that routes every request through OllamaEndpointRegistry instead of a fixed HttpClient.BaseAddress. Registered on all typed HttpClients that talk to Ollama (OllamaService, DraftModelCapacityClient, PromptAssessor, TaskClassifier, and the context pipeline stages) so a single registry/config change (multiple `Endpoints`, failover/round-robin/explicit selection) affects every caller without touching their code. Each typed client still gets a BaseAddress at registration (pointing at the legacy/default OllamaUrl) purely as a fallback for the rare case the registry has no endpoints; in normal operation this handler always overwrites scheme/host/port with the selected endpoint's URL before the request is sent. Callers that want a specific endpoint (e.g. CleanAndChat's optional endpointName parameter) attach it via HttpRequestOptionsKey on the request; this handler reads it and passes it through to SelectEndpoint.

name: McpContextService
summary: Generates MCP tool context summaries at three verbosity levels based on the current task type, so the calling AI gets exactly as much detail as useful: Planning → Full: all tools with descriptions, grouped by category Code/Debug/Refactor/Test/Review → Brief: category names + tool list, no descriptions General/Explain → Mention: single-line reminder that tools exist

name: GetContextBlock
summary: Returns the MCP context block to append to the cleaned context for a given task type. Returns an empty string if there is nothing worth adding (shouldn't happen in practice).

name: ProviderAutoRegistrationService
summary: Formerly a background service that waited for DraftModel to warm up, then wrote this MCP server's entry into every detected AI provider config (Continue, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Sixth, etc.) on every startup. That auto-write behavior is removed — AiProviderConfigService no longer detects or writes any provider configs, so this service now no-ops immediately instead of waiting on DraftModel for no payoff. Use the "TokenSaver: Open Install Prompt" VS Code command (or read `INSTALL_PROMPT.md` directly) to wire up a provider manually instead.

name: UnhandledFaultTracker
summary: Tracks the most recent unhandled exception thrown while processing a request (MCP tools/call or any other HTTP endpoint on this server), so `/health` can report degraded status even when every other health check (DraftModel reachability, etc.) still passes. Mirrors DraftModel.Loader's `ModelHealthMonitor.RecordFault`/`HasRecentFault` design: a stack trace on the server isn't something a liveness probe can detect on its own — the process is still up and answering requests — so it's surfaced as a time-boxed signal instead. Only the exception's message is retained (not the full stack trace) since this value is expected to be surfaced in a health response body.

name: FaultTtl
summary: How long a recorded fault keeps HasRecentFault true before aging out.

name: ClearFault
summary: Clears any recorded fault immediately — used by tests; not called from production code paths.

name: WorkspaceRootResolver
summary: Auto-detects the workspace root by walking up from a starting directory to the nearest repo root (a directory containing a .sln/.slnx file or a .git folder). Pulled out of `Program.cs` so the composition root doesn't embed directory-walking logic inline.

name: FindRepoRoot
summary: Walks up from searchFrom looking for a repo root. Returns the first matching directory's full path, or `null` if none is found before running out of parent directories. Callers always walk up (not just when a workspace root is unset) because some launchers (e.g. the VS Code extension) pass a project sub-folder rather than the repo root.

name: AccuracyTestTools
summary: Workflow: AgentConfig(action: 'test') → AgentConfig(action: 'get') → AgentConfig(action: 'update') Stage proposals first with AgentConfig(action: 'save'), then apply them with 'update'.

name: DevLoopTools
summary: Dev-loop shell-out tools whose raw output is usually pure noise: container logs, test runs, lint, build-log tailing, git diffs. Every one of these follows the same shape: run the thing, retain the raw output on disk (RawArtifactWriter), distill it with a role-specific prompt (DistillationService), return the compact result plus a pointer to the full artifact. Windows/Docker-Desktop oriented (ContainerLogs shells out to the `docker` CLI rather than depending on a Docker SDK package) — see TokenSaver/docs/token-economy-tools-contract.md for per-tool degraded behavior when the underlying command isn't available.

name: RunProcessOutputOnlyAsync
summary: Runs an external process to completion and returns combined stdout (stderr appended on non-zero exit). Used by tools that don't need the exit code separately (git diff, docker logs).

name: Task
summary: Runs an external process to completion, returning its exit code and captured stdout/stderr separately.

name: SemanticIndexTools
summary: Chunk-level semantic index/search — deliberately separate from CodeHelperTools.CodeIndex (which does exact/substring symbol-name search via WorkspaceIndexService). This is for natural-language queries ("where do we retry a failed Ollama call") where a function/ section-level summary is more useful than an exact symbol name match. See TokenSaver/docs/token-economy-tools-contract.md.

name: SessionTools
summary: Session context snapshot/restore, extending the existing CONTEXT.md pattern. A large incoming blob is distilled before being stored as the "quick restore" — restoring a stale multi-thousand-token dump would defeat the point of a concise-context tool — while the full blob is kept alongside on disk for when detail is actually needed (SessionRestore's full:true). See TokenSaver/docs/token-economy-tools-contract.md.

name: TokenEconomyTools
summary: Measurement/routing tools for the token-economy design: TokenBudget (pure, no LLM), ModelRoute (task_type → model routing table), TokenSavingsReport/WorthKeeping (query the savings history recorded by DistillationService via ISavingsTracker). See TokenSaver/docs/token-economy-tools-contract.md.

name: DegradedHealthTests
summary: Covers the two ways TokenSaver.MCP's /health can report degraded status: an unhandled exception recorded by FaultTrackingMiddleware/UnhandledFaultTracker, and a failing SelfTestHealthCheck check. Mirrors DraftModel.Loader.Tests's DegradedHealthTests — same two mechanisms, same "shouldn't affect /health/ready" boundary, adapted to this project's ASP.NET Core health-checks-based architecture instead of a hand-rolled HttpListener. Note: unlike DraftModel's router, ASP.NET Core's HealthCheckMiddleware maps HealthStatus.Degraded to HTTP 200 by default (only Unhealthy maps to 503) — these tests assert on the JSON body's "status" field rather than expecting a non-200 status code.

name: HealthTestHost
summary: Minimal, purpose-built ASP.NET Core test host for the degraded-health/self-test feature — deliberately does NOT reuse the real Program.cs composition root, which wires up ~20 singletons, background index warm-up, and real DraftModel connectivity waits that would make these tests slow and flaky for something that's really just "does the fault-tracking middleware + these two health checks behave correctly". Wires only what that needs: FaultTrackingMiddleware, UnhandledFaultHealthCheck, SelfTestHealthCheck, the real /health and /health/ready mappings (same shape as Program.cs), and a throw-on-demand test endpoint to trigger real unhandled exceptions the same way a real MCP tools/call failure would.

name: TokenEconomyToolsTests
summary: TokenBudget is the one method on TokenEconomyTools that never calls Ollama (pure EstimateTokens math), so it's testable end-to-end through the actual tool class without a live model — exactly the gap CLAUDE.md's "Known gaps" section flags for every existing Tools/*.cs class (zero tests today). ModelRoute/TokenSavingsReport/WorthKeeping need a live Ollama process and/or a populated savings history and are covered instead at the service level (DistillationServiceTests, SavingsTrackerTests in TokenSaver.Library.Tests).
